title: Garrison: A High-Performance GPU-Accelerated Inference System for Adversarial Ensemble Defense
problem: Deploying adversarial ensemble defense methods (multiple DNNs for robustness) on DNN inference systems is inefficient and impractical due to the inherent dynamics and randomness of ensemble approaches. Existing inference systems cannot effectively manage the resource requirements and latency constraints of concurrent ensemble model execution.
motivation: Adversarial attacks pose critical threats to deep learning systems, and adversarial ensemble defense is a proven effective robustness technique, yet current inference systems cannot efficiently support ensemble deployments.
method: Garrison employs a multi-granularity GPU partitioning strategy that optimizes hardware utilization by exploiting GPU heterogeneity using Multi-Instance GPUs. It integrates a reinforcement learning-based scheduling mechanism to coordinate random ensembles of diverse defense models, enhancing robustness while maintaining bounded latency. The system intelligently manages resource allocation and scheduling to handle ensemble randomness efficiently.
key_novelty: Combination of multi-granularity GPU partitioning with RL-based scheduling specifically optimized for adversarial ensemble defense using Multi-Instance GPUs.
contributions: Garrison inference system specifically designed for efficient adversarial ensemble defense deployment
Multi-granularity GPU partitioning strategy exploiting GPU heterogeneity for improved utilization
Reinforcement learning-based scheduling for coordinating random ensemble models with bounded latency
6.6X speedup and 24.5% adversarial robustness improvement over state-of-the-art inference frameworks
